chapter: Handedness and Gene Austin in California
title: Playing with Austin at the Coconut Grove
summary: Austin plays in the black keys, Hazel solves it by pulling his horn out, and the small band outdraws Gus Arnheim's big band.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: I played the foot, yeah. And then the whole cornet with my hands. Well, you see the thing with Austin over there. We only had four pieces, you see. And they built a special stand and pushed it back against the band, regular bandstand. Gus Ornheim had the band in there while we were out there. And we'd just play intermissions. We played ten minutes five times a night. And three times Austin would sing a couple of songs with us. And we'd play a few tunes. He played that, you ever seen him play, roll the piano in the back of his fist like that? That's the way, yeah, that's the way he played. For a kick. He plays in the black keys. There's another funny story too. We got out there and we started rehearsing. I couldn't get with him, you know. I said, man, what key you playing? What key you playing in? He says, I'm playing in the black key. I'm playing in the black keys. So I tried for half an hour. I just couldn't get anywhere near him, you know. I couldn't play in the keys. He was playing. He was playing in B natural, E natural, F sharp, C sharp, you know. So finally I told him, I said, Mr. You might as well buy me a ticket and send me back home. I can't make this. He said, what do you mean you can't make it? I said, well, I just can't make it. I said, I can't play in those keys. I said, you get my keys, but he couldn't play in my keys. So he told me, finally he says, I don't know, I don't see how you can't do it. Wingy did it. You see, so I said, oh, oh, oh. If Wingy done it, there's a trick to it somewhere. Because I know Wingy can't really know as big as his head. So I said, if Wingy did it, there's a trick to it somewhere, you see. So I kept fooling around. So finally I pulled the horn out in E, you see. And he was playing some of these days. So he started to end up. Well, that put me in the same as in the key of F. The finger was the same as the key of F. But the horn was out. Instead of being flat, it's out there, you see. So I had it. So I said, go ahead. Blow, mister. Go ahead. Do anything you want. I got you now. You blowing with me now. But I was just about ready to pack up and come back home, you know. So we'd, like I tell you, we'd play five times a night, just ten minutes. And then we had a job in the afternoon. There's a place in the back of the Coconut Grove called Aledo. It's an open air thing. They put on fashion shows and things like that out there, you see. And we worked out there. I'll tell you about this later. But anyhow, in the Grove there, the times that Austin didn't play, well, we'd just go up there and just flew around. We'd play the muskrat and Panama and bugle call them, things like that. And the guys and the gals back in the bed. Onheim had a great big man, about 18 men. And they'd holler tunes for us to play, you know. And it was funny, Bill. The first night we were in there, when Onheim would play, a few people would get up and dance, you know. But when we'd get up there and play, man, everybody looked like everybody wanted to get up. And the Meta D and the Headwaters, they were trying to shove the people off the floor. They weren't supposed to dance to us, you see. They were trying to shove them off. Well, about the second night, the boss, there was a fellow by the name of Franks, walks down and he sees them. He sees them trying to shove them people off the floor. And he hollers to the Meta, what are you doing? He said, well, they want to dance tomorrow. I said, well, let them people dance. What do you want to shove them off? The big band can't make them dance, and they make them dance? Let them dance. So they'd get out there and dance when we played. And the kids back there would be, I was Panama, Tyrae. You know?
